summary: The UAE is now AGENCY-CONFIRMED PROHIBITED for private roof rats, and it is a textbook species-not-domestication case. The Ministry of Climate Change and Environment (MOCCAE) confirmed in writing (June 2026) that the 'domesticated rats' exemption to the rodent-keeping restriction under Federal Law No. 22 of 2016 applies STRICTLY to the fancy rat (Rattus norvegicus). Because the roof rat (R. rattus) is not classified as a domesticated pet under UAE regulations, private individuals may not keep, breed, possess, or import it; the only import pathway is for licensed research entities or zoological facilities. (An earlier reading that the exemption might cover domesticated R. rattus is closed by MOCCAE's species-specific reply.)
agency_confirmations: UAE Ministry of Climate Change and Environment (MOCCAE), written reply June 2026: the 'domesticated rats' exemption to the rodent-keeping restriction under Federal Law No. 22 of 2016 applies STRICTLY to the fancy rat (Rattus norvegicus). The roof rat (Rattus rattus) is not classified as a domesticated pet under UAE regulations, so private individuals may not keep, breed, possess, or import it; importation is restricted to licensed research entities or zoological facilities.

kit.problem: The UAE bars private individuals from keeping most rodents but exempts 'domesticated rats'. MOCCAE has confirmed it reads that exemption to mean only the fancy rat (Rattus norvegicus). A captive-bred, domesticated roof rat (R. rattus) is therefore prohibited to keep, breed, or import, even though it is equally domesticated. This is a classification gap, not a safety judgment.
kit.ask: Ask MOCCAE to recognize captive-bred, multi-generation domesticated Rattus rattus as a 'domesticated rat' within the existing Federal Law No. 22 of 2016 exemption (the same exemption the fancy rat holds), or to set out a private-keeper pathway. The animals are tame, indoor-kept, and never released. The already-permitted fancy rat is itself the wild brown rat (R. norvegicus), domesticated only in the 19th century (see https://blonderoofrat.com/how-the-sewer-rat-became-the-fancy-rat/), so a captive-bred R. rattus is the same case one species over.
kit.branch_note: MOCCAE confirmed this is its classification under the regulation, so the lever is the agency/regulator. Ask MOCCAE to read the 'domesticated rats' exemption to include domesticated R. rattus, an interpretation or classification change. If MOCCAE states that only a regulatory amendment can do it, that points to the rule-making authority. It is not a courts matter.

template.en:
To the Ministry of Climate Change and Environment,

Under Federal Law No. 22 of 2016, individuals may keep 'domesticated rats', but I understand the Ministry currently reads this to cover only the fancy rat (Rattus norvegicus), excluding the domesticated roof rat (Rattus rattus).

I respectfully ask the Ministry to recognize captive-bred, multi-generation domesticated Rattus rattus as a 'domesticated rat' within this exemption, the same way the fancy rat is treated. These animals are selectively bred for tameness over many generations, kept indoors as companion animals, and never released; they pose no greater risk than the fancy rat already permitted.

If recognition requires a regulatory step, I would be grateful to know the process. Thank you for your consideration.

[Your name]
template.ar:
إلى وزارة التغير المناخي والبيئة الموقرة،

بموجب القانون الاتحادي رقم 22 لسنة 2016، يُسمح للأفراد بتربية «الجرذان المستأنسة»، إلا أنني أتفهم أن الوزارة تفسّر ذلك حالياً على أنه يشمل فقط الجرذ النرويجي (Rattus norvegicus)، مع استثناء الجرذ الأسود المستأنس (Rattus rattus).

أرجو من الوزارة الكريمة الاعتراف بالجرذ الأسود (Rattus rattus) المربّى في الأسر عبر أجيال متعددة باعتباره «جرذاً مستأنساً» ضمن هذا الاستثناء، تماماً كما يُعامَل الجرذ النرويجي. فهذه الحيوانات تُنتخب للأُلفة عبر أجيال عديدة، وتُربّى داخل المنازل كحيوانات أليفة، ولا تُطلق في البيئة أبداً، وهي لا تشكّل خطراً أكبر من الجرذ النرويجي المسموح به بالفعل.

وإذا كان هذا الاعتراف يتطلب إجراءً تنظيمياً، فسأكون ممتناً لمعرفة الآلية. شكراً لكم على حسن اهتمامكم.

[الاسم]

restrictions.summary: Keeping a domesticated roof rat is exempt from the UAE dangerous-animal ban (no keeper permit). Commercial breeding/selling needs a MOCCAE animal-care-activities licence + a local commercial licence; importing needs a MOCCAE live-animal import permit (AED 100) + the rodent veterinary health certificate. ⚠️ Confirm with MOCCAE that 'domesticated rats' in the Annex covers captive-bred R. rattus. Never release.

inquiry_focus: (1) Does the Annex 1 exemption under Federal Law No. 22 of 2016 for 'domesticated rats and mice' apply to Rattus rattus (roof/black rat) kept as captive-bred pets, or only to R. norvegicus — is there a ministerial circular clarifying species scope? (2) For a private individual importing a small number of captive-bred R. rattus as pets, does the MOCCAE live-animal import permit apply, and is a facility/breeding-centre licence required, or is there a private-owner pathway like the cat/dog import permit? (3) For small-scale private hobby breeding/occasional rehoming (no commercial intent), is any MOCCAE or municipality licence required, or does the Annex exemption fully cover private possession without registration?
